thread:
Asha (support): forwarding a customer escalation — their rerank calls started returning 5xx and 504s under steady load this morning. p95 token latency shot up from ~220ms to >2.5s and then gateway timeouts from our edge. customer says it started after a spike in query volume around 09:12 UTC.

Eve (customer): here’s an example request we send (we batch ~400 queries every 30s):

Eve (customer): ```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3", ..., "q400"],
  "candidates": [["c1","c2",...], ...],
  "model": "rwd-re-rank-v1"
}
```

Eve (customer): responses initially slow, then many come back as 504 or 502. x-request-id headers vary. No auth failures.

Mike (eng-runtime): thanks Asha — we saw similar alerts on our side: several rerank pools hit high CPU / stall on the attention kernels when candidate counts > 128 and long token sequences. OpsBot triggered a capacity alarm at 09:14.

OpsBot: [ALERT] rerank-pool-3 cpu_pct=92% p95_latency=2540ms gateway_timeouts=37 since 09:12 UTC

Lee (oncall): can someone paste the gateway logs for 09:12-09:20? I want to confirm if the gateway returned 504 or if upstream returned 5xx.

Jordan (sre): digging — gateway returned 504s (timeout waiting for backend) in most cases. Backend logs show multiple 5xx entries (502 / 500) around same time. Looks like the inference workers hit long GC/IO stalls when candidate arrays were large. Found repeated stack traces pointing to token-buffer growth in rerank worker.

Jordan (sre): sample backend log snippet:```
[2026-04-12T09:13:27.482Z] ERROR worker-17 request_id=abc123 host=rt-3 msg="handler error" code=500 detail="oom when allocating attention buffer for batch=384 seq_len=1024 candidates_per_query=48"
[2026-04-12T09:13:27.483Z] WARN worker-17 request_id=abc123 retry_attempts=1
```

Mike (eng-runtime): candidate_per_query=48 with queries=384 => effectively huge token blowup (384*48*seq_len). If KV cache + attention buffers grow beyond available GPU memory we start thrashing and then crash or OOM. The gateway waits and then times out -> 504.

Asha (support): customer claims they always used these batch sizes. They’re on Dedicated — expecting stable throughput. They want a root cause and mitigation.

Lee (oncall): quick repro — I launched a small test against staging pool with similar batch/candidate sizes. Reproduced p95 spike and occasional 502s. Repro commands:```
# minimal repro script (pseudo)
for i in range(200):
  POST /v1/rerank 
  body=large_batch(queries=384, candidates=48)
  sleep(0.2)
```

Lee (oncall): observed GPU mem climbing then eviction and backend restart.

Mike (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation options:
- add request validation: reject requests with queries * candidates > 20000 (return 400)
- set per-pool circuit breaker to throttle large concurrent rerank batches
- route heavy rerank traffic to larger instance types temporarily

Jordan (sre): also saw our gateway was configured with upstream_timeout=60s; some customers hit that and got 504s after long retries. We should ensure clients get early 413/400 instead of causing worker OOMs.

Eve (customer): we can change client but need RC from you — can you add server-side limits? We can reduce batch to 128 queries and 16 candidates but that’s a product regression for us.

Mike (eng-runtime): agreed we should deploy a validation layer quickly. I’ll open a runtime PR to: validate candidate counts, add heuristic estimating token blowup (queries*candidates*avg_tokens) and reject if estimate > threshold. Also adding graceful failure path: return 429 with Retry-After when pool is saturated instead of letting it OOM.

Asha (support): customer prefers 429+Retry-After so their client can backoff automatically. They want us to notify when fix is live.

Jordan (sre): temp workaround: increased rerank pool capacity for that customer’s Dedicated pool (scaled +2 GPUs) and enabled pool-level throttling to 4 concurrent large batches. That reduced the 5xx rate to near-zero.

OpsBot: [CHANGE] scaled rerank-pool-7 +2 gpus for customer-acme (applied by jordan)

Lee (oncall): follow-up items (short):
- Mike: validation PR + canary deploy to prod (rollback safe)
- SRE: keep scaled capacity for 24h and monitor p95, 5xx, OOMs
- Support: communicate guidance to customer: recommended batch sizing + fallbacks

Mike (eng-runtime): created PR #4821 — includes server-side validation, circuit-breaker and `estimate_token_blowup` heuristic. Will canary in 30m to a small percent of traffic.

Mike (eng-runtime): PR snippet:```
if estimate_token_blowup(req) > MAX_TOKENS:
  return 400, {"error":"request too large: reduce queries/candidates or decrease seq_len"}
```

Asha (support): sent note to customer with temporary mitigations and ETA for fix. They replied: "Thanks — we can throttle down to 200 q / 16 c for now. Please ping when it’s live."

Jordan (sre): monitoring update (10:15): after scale + throttles p95 down to 320ms, gateway_timeouts -> 2, 5xx->1 in last 15m. Looks stable. Will continue to watch for 6h.

Lee (oncall): long-term: we should add better observability around request-level token estimates and surface candidate counts on dashboards. Also consider per-customer max candidates default.

Mike (eng-runtime): will follow up with a postmortem once PR is fully deployed. Immediate action: canary the validation and set default per-tenant limit = 1024*1024 token-estimate (tunable).

Asha (support): resolving for now as "mitigated". Will reopen if customer sees more 5xxs. :thumbsup:

Eve (customer): thanks team, appreciate the quick response.

Jordan (sre): marking incident as Sev-2 -> follow-up required.

Lee (oncall): action items summarized in thread, assigning owners. Closing thread for notifications. :white_check_mark:
